tasks.title: Port 0
tasks.statement:
Bind a TcpListener to 127.0.0.1:0, take the port from local_addr() and print "port above zero: true".

Expected output:
`port above zero: true`
tasks.hint: TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await?.local_addr()?.port()

tasks.title: The server accepted a client
tasks.statement:
Run a server in a task: it accepts one connection and prints "connected". The client in main connects (TcpStream::connect). Wait for the server task.

Expected output:
`connected`
tasks.hint: Get the address from listener.local_addr() before spawn.

tasks.title: Send and read
tasks.statement:
The client sends "hello" and closes the connection. The server reads to the end (read_to_end) and prints "received: hello".

Expected output:
`received: hello`
tasks.hint: Drop the client — the server will get EOF.

tasks.title: read returned 0
tasks.statement:
The client connects and closes the connection at once. The server calls read once and prints «EOF: n», where n is the number of bytes read.

Expected output:
EOF: 0
tasks.hint: A connection closed by the peer: read returns Ok(0).

tasks.title: Echo for one message
tasks.statement:
The server reads up to 64 bytes (one read) and sends them back. The client sends «ping», reads the reply and prints «echo: ping».

Expected output:
echo: ping
tasks.hint: Server: let n = s.read(&mut buf).await?; s.write_all(&buf[..n]).await?.

tasks.title: Echo server for many
tasks.statement:
Write a server with an accept loop and a spawn per client: the handler reads and writes back until it gets EOF. Three clients connect one after another, send "id N", read the reply and print "echo N" for N = 0, 1, 2.

Expected output:
`echo 0`
`echo 1`
`echo 2`
tasks.hint: loop { let (s, _) = l.accept().await?; tokio::spawn(handle(s)); } — run the server in a separate task.

tasks.title: Reading line by line
tasks.statement:
The server sends the client «a\nb\nc\n» and closes the connection. The client reads with BufReader::lines() and prints each line.

Expected output:
a
b
c
tasks.hint: use tokio::io::{AsyncBufReadExt, BufReader}; BufReader::new(c).lines(); next_line().await.

tasks.title: read_line and counting bytes
tasks.statement:
The client sends «hello\nworld\n» and closes the connection. The server calls read_line in a loop and prints «N: line», where N is the number of bytes (with the newline), and «EOF» at the end of the stream.

Expected output:
6: hello
6: world
EOF
tasks.hint: let n = reader.read_line(&mut s).await?; if n == 0 { break }

tasks.title: Length prefix
tasks.statement:
The client sends a frame: 4 bytes of length (big-endian) and then "hello". The server reads the header (read_exact for 4 bytes), then exactly that many bytes of data and prints "length 5, data hello".

Expected output:
`length 5, data hello`
tasks.hint: u32::from_be_bytes(hdr) as usize; (5u32).to_be_bytes().

tasks.title: read_u32 and write_u32
tasks.statement:
The client sends the number 256 with write_u32 (big-endian). The server reads it with read_u32 and prints it.

Expected output:
256
tasks.hint: AsyncWriteExt::write_u32 and AsyncReadExt::read_u32 use network byte order.

tasks.title: into_split
tasks.statement:
An echo server (reads and writes back). The client splits the socket with into_split(): a writer task sends "split", the main task reads exactly 5 bytes (read_exact) and prints "answer: split".

Expected output:
`answer: split`
tasks.hint: let (mut r, mut w) = c.into_split(); tokio::spawn(async move { w.write_all(..).await });

tasks.title: shutdown of the write side
tasks.statement:
The client sends "request", closes the write side (shutdown), then reads the reply to the end. The server reads to the end of the request, replies "ok" and closes. The client prints "answer: ok".

Expected output:
`answer: ok`
tasks.hint: c.shutdown().await closes the write side; the server's read_to_end will finish.

tasks.title: Connection refused
tasks.statement:
Bind a listener, find out its address and drop the listener. An attempt at TcpStream::connect to this address must end with an error. Print its kind with {:?}: e.kind().

Expected output:
ConnectionRefused
tasks.hint: match TcpStream::connect(addr).await { Err(e) => println!("{:?}", e.kind()), .. }

tasks.title: UDP: echo
tasks.statement:
A server on a UdpSocket (bind 127.0.0.1:0) receives a datagram with recv_from and sends it back to the sender. The client sends "ping" and prints "answer: ping".

Expected output:
`answer: ping`
tasks.hint: let (n, from) = s.recv_from(&mut buf).await?; s.send_to(&buf[..n], from).await?;

tasks.title: Datagram boundaries
tasks.statement:
From one UDP socket send «ab» and «cd» to another with two send_to calls. The receiver makes two recv_from calls and prints each datagram on its own line.

Expected output:
ab
cd
tasks.hint: One send — one read, no merging.

tasks.title: Read timeout
tasks.statement:
The server accepts a connection and stays silent (holds the socket for 300 ms). The client tries to read with a 50 ms timeout and on error prints "read timeout".

Expected output:
`read timeout`
tasks.hint: tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_millis(50), c.read(&mut buf)).await

tasks.title: Stopping the accept loop
tasks.statement:
An accept loop in a task with select!: either accept a client (count it) or receive a stop signal over oneshot. One client connects, then (after a 50 ms pause) the signal is sent. The task prints "accepted: 1" and "stopped".

Expected output:
`accepted: 1`
`stopped`
tasks.hint: select! { r = l.accept() => { r.unwrap(); n += 1; }, _ = &mut stop => break }

tasks.title: Counting connections
tasks.statement:
The server accepts exactly 5 connections in a loop and counts them in an AtomicUsize (each in its own spawn task). Five clients connect. Wait for the server and print "connections: 5".

Expected output:
`connections: 5`
tasks.hint: for _ in 0..5 { let (s, _) = l.accept().await?; counter.fetch_add(1, SeqCst); spawn(..) }

tasks.title: io::copy
tasks.statement:
Copy the bytes from a &[u8] slice (b"hello world") into a Vec<u8> with tokio::io::copy and print "copied: N".

Expected output:
`copied: 11`
tasks.hint: let mut r: &[u8] = b"hello world"; let mut w = Vec::new(); tokio::io::copy(&mut r, &mut w).await?

tasks.title: duplex in memory
tasks.statement:
Create a pair tokio::io::duplex(64). Write «hi» into one half, close it and read everything from the other into a String. Print the string.

Expected output:
hi
tasks.hint: let (mut a, mut b) = tokio::io::duplex(64); drop(a) after writing; b.read_to_string(&mut s).

tasks.title: A proxy with copy_bidirectional
tasks.statement:
An echo server, a proxy and a client. The proxy accepts the client's connection, connects to the echo server and pumps data in both directions with tokio::io::copy_bidirectional. The client sends "via proxy", reads the same number of bytes and prints "via proxy: via proxy".

Expected output:
`via proxy: via proxy`
tasks.hint: copy_bidirectional(&mut client_side, &mut upstream).await — in a separate task.

tasks.title: Stream: map and collect
tasks.statement:
From tokio_stream::iter(1..=3) get a stream, multiply each value by 2 (map) and collect into a Vec (collect). Print the vector with {:?}.

Expected output:
[2, 4, 6]
tasks.hint: use tokio_stream::{self as stream, StreamExt}; stream::iter(..).map(..).collect::<Vec<_>>().await

tasks.title: ReceiverStream
tasks.statement:
Wrap the receiver of an mpsc channel in a ReceiverStream, send 1, 2, 3 from a task and collect the stream into a vector. Print the vector with {:?}.

Expected output:
[1, 2, 3]
tasks.hint: tokio_stream::wrappers::ReceiverStream::new(rx).collect::<Vec<_>>().await

tasks.title: Stream: filter and take
tasks.statement:
From iter(1..=10) keep the even numbers (filter), take the first three (take) and collect into a Vec. Print the vector with {:?}.

Expected output:
[2, 4, 6]
tasks.hint: .filter(|x| x % 2 == 0).take(3).collect::<Vec<_>>().await

tasks.title: tokio::fs
tasks.statement:
Write «hello» to the file /tmp/say_r36.txt with tokio::fs::write, read it back with read_to_string, print the contents and delete the file (remove_file).

Expected output:
hello
tasks.hint: tokio::fs::write(path, data).await?; tokio::fs::read_to_string(path).await?

tasks.title: spawn_blocking
tasks.statement:
With tokio::task::spawn_blocking compute the sum of the numbers from 1 to 1_000_000 (u64) and print the result.

Expected output:
500000500000
tasks.hint: spawn_blocking(|| (1..=1_000_000u64).sum::<u64>()).await?

tasks.title: lookup_host
tasks.statement:
With tokio::net::lookup_host("127.0.0.1:80") get the addresses and print "addresses: N".

Expected output:
`addresses: 1`
tasks.hint: lookup_host(..).await?.count()

tasks.title: The client's address
tasks.statement:
The server gets the client's address from accept() and prints "loopback client: true" if addr.ip().is_loopback().

Expected output:
`loopback client: true`
tasks.hint: let (_s, peer) = l.accept().await?; peer.ip().is_loopback()

tasks.title: Unix socket
tasks.statement:
Bind a UnixListener to /tmp/say_r36.sock, connect with a UnixStream client, send «ping», the server reads and prints «unix: ping». Delete the socket file when done.

Expected output:
unix: ping
tasks.hint: use tokio::net::{UnixListener, UnixStream}; delete the old file before bind (let _ = std::fs::remove_file).

tasks.title: A text protocol
tasks.statement:
The server reads the line «ADD 2 3», adds the numbers and replies with a line containing the result and a newline. The client sends «ADD 2 3\n», reads the reply line and prints it without the newline.

Expected output:
5
tasks.hint: BufReader::new(socket).read_line(..); split_whitespace(); write_all(format!("{}\n", sum)).
